content.title: Section IV – Visiting Our Social Media Profiles
paragraphs: We maintain publicly accessible social media profiles on Instagram and Facebook (so-called fan pages), through which we communicate with guests and interested parties and provide information about our studio apartments, offers and news. The provider of both platforms is Meta Platforms Ireland Limited, 4 Grand Canal Square, Grand Canal Harbour, Dublin 2, Ireland (“Meta”). Instagram and Facebook are Meta products.

content.title: 17. Social Media Presences (Instagram and Facebook)
paragraphs: Joint controllership (Art. 26 GDPR): Under data protection law, the operation of our profiles on Instagram and Facebook constitutes joint controllership within the meaning of Art. 26 GDPR. This means that Charlie M as the profile operator and Meta as the platform operator are jointly responsible for the processing of users’ personal data in connection with the respective profile, in particular for the processing of so-called Insights data. Accordingly, we have concluded an agreement on joint controllership with Meta (the so-called Page Insights Controller Addendum), which applies to all Meta products used by us (Instagram and Facebook). You can view the agreement at the following link: https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms/page_controller_addendum

Under this agreement, Meta assumes primary responsibility for the processing of the Insights data. This applies in particular to the information obligations and data subject rights regulated in Art. 12 to 22 GDPR and to the obligations set out in Art. 32 to 34 GDPR to ensure data security and to report data protection breaches. Meta has also made the essential content of this agreement available in accordance with Art. 26(2) GDPR at the following link: https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms/page_controller_addendum

Please note that you use our social media profiles and their functions at your own responsibility. This applies in particular to the use of the interactive functions (e.g. commenting, sharing, rating, liking, messaging).
Scope and purpose of the joint processing: The following data processing operations take place in connection with our Instagram and Facebook profiles:

Reports/statistics (Page Insights): In connection with the operation of our social media profiles, we use the analysis functions provided there in order to obtain statistical evaluations of the use of our Instagram and Facebook profiles (so-called Page Insights). For this purpose, cookies and similar technologies from Meta are used when our profiles are visited, and a unique user ID is created in each case. For users who are logged in to Instagram or Facebook at the time of the page visit, this user ID is assigned to their account. For users who are not logged in or not registered, the user ID is not assigned to an account.

Categories of data: The Page Insights contain information about the reach of and interactions with our posts, about users’ actions on our profiles, demographic data (age, gender, location), information about visits to and interactions with our profiles and about the long-term performance of our individual posts. An overview of the Page Insights can be viewed at https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms/page_controller_addendum. These statistics are created by Meta on the basis of certain events that are logged by Meta’s servers when people interact with our profiles and the content associated with them. This logging is carried out solely by Meta. We have neither access to the personal data underlying these statistics nor any influence on its collection.

Purpose: Meta processes the aforementioned information, among other things, to improve its own advertising system. On this basis, Meta provides us as the profile operator with anonymous visitor statistics. These statistics show us, for example, which posts are viewed or shared particularly often and from which regions and age groups our visitors come. We use this information to continuously improve our social media profiles and their content and to make them more interesting. We receive the statistics exclusively in anonymised form. We have no access to the underlying personal data and cannot draw any conclusions about individual users.

Legal basis: The legal basis for this processing is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interests). Our legitimate interest lies in the optimised presentation of our company and our offerings. You may object to the processing of your data based on Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR under the conditions of Art. 21 GDPR (on the right to object, see Section 20).
Communication: If you are registered on Instagram or Facebook, you can comment on our posts, send us private messages or interact with our content and posts in other ways.
Categories of data: In this context, we may receive further information, e.g. through user comments, private messages or because you follow us or share our content.

Purpose: This data is processed exclusively for the purpose of communicating and interacting with you. Insofar as you provide us with personal data via a user comment or a private message, we process this data exclusively in order to respond to your enquiry and to communicate with you.

Legal basis: The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interests). We have a legitimate interest in responding to your messages via the channel you have chosen. You may object to the processing of your data based on Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR under the conditions of Art. 21 GDPR (on the right to object, see Section 20).

Further processing by Meta: In addition to the Page Insights described above, Meta collects further information when its social media platforms are visited, which is collected on your device via cookies or similar technologies and transmitted to Meta (e.g. IP address, browser type, language settings). Meta uses this information, among other things, to create user profiles based on your preferences and interests and to display advertising tailored to them. Meta may also share the data collected in connection with our profiles with other companies of the Meta group of companies and with advertising and marketing partners, for example to improve advertisements or for measurement purposes. This also applies to all other Instagram and Facebook profiles. On the basis of this data, content or advertising can be offered tailored to you. If you wish to avoid this, you should log out of the respective service or deactivate the “stay logged in” function and delete the cookies stored on your device.

Objection options: Users of Facebook and Instagram can also influence, under the settings for advertising preferences (https://www.facebook.com/ads/preferences), the extent to which their user behaviour may be recorded when visiting our Facebook page or Instagram profile. Further options for objecting are:

As the profile operator, we have neither influence over nor complete knowledge of how Meta uses the data from visits to our profiles for its own purposes, the extent to which activities are assigned to individual users, how long Meta stores this data or whether data is passed on to third parties.

Storage period: As a rule, we do not ourselves store any personal data relating to communications and interactions with users that take place via our social media profiles. Your public interactions (e.g. comments, likes) remain visible on the respective platform until you remove them yourself. For the period for which the data is stored by Meta, please refer to Meta’s privacy policy: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy

Recipients and third-country transfers: The purposes for which and the extent to which Meta processes the data collected via our profiles and passes it on to third parties – possibly outside the European Union and the European Economic Area – are described by Meta in its data policy.

It is also possible that some of the information collected by Meta is processed outside the European Union, in the USA. Insofar as personal data is transferred to and stored on Meta servers in the USA, the recipient is generally Meta Platforms, Inc., 1 Hacker Way, Menlo Park, CA 94025, USA. For data transfers to the USA and other third countries, compliance with data protection standards and your rights is, according to Meta, ensured by appropriate safeguards (e.g. EU standard contractual clauses pursuant to Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 of the European Commission (Art. 46(2)(c) GDPR)). Further information on data protection can be found at https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy.

Note on your rights: If you would like information about how Meta processes your data, or if you wish to exercise your other data subject rights, including your right to object, the most effective way to do so is directly with Meta. Only Meta has access to the users’ Insights data mentioned above and can directly take appropriate measures and provide information. If you nevertheless need assistance, you can contact us using the contact details provided under Section 2.

content.title: 19. General Information on Storage Periods
paragraphs: Unless an explicit storage period is specified in this privacy notice, personal data is stored for as long as is necessary for the purpose for which it was collected; the data is then deleted or anonymised. Storage beyond this only takes place

if this is necessary to fulfil legal obligations. Insofar as we are legally obliged to retain data, we store your data for the legally prescribed period. Legal requirements regarding storage may arise in particular from the retention periods of the German Commercial Code (HGB) or the German Fiscal Code (AO), in particular from section 147 AO and sections 238, 257 HGB. The retention period under these provisions is generally between 6 years (in particular for commercial and business letters and other documents relevant for taxation) and 8 years (in particular for accounting records) from the end of the year in which the commercial or business letter was received or sent, the accounting record was created or the relevant transaction was completed, e.g. we have conclusively processed your enquiry.

if the data is needed for longer for criminal prosecution or for the assertion, exercise or defence of legal claims, including for documentation and evidence purposes. In that case, the data is stored until the matter in question and any mutual claims have been fully resolved, taking into account the statutory limitation period.

For processing operations that we carry out on the basis of your consent, the data is deleted when you withdraw your consent or at an earlier point in time when the data is no longer necessary for the purpose for which we collected it.

content.title: 20. Your Rights as a Data Subject
paragraphs: If you wish to exercise the rights described below, please contact us using the contact details provided under Section 2.

Right of access: Under the conditions of Art. 15 GDPR, you may at any time request information about the personal data relating to you that we process, in particular about the purposes of processing, the categories of data, the recipients, the storage period, the origin of the data, the existence of automated decision-making including profiling, and your data subject rights. You may also request a copy of your personal data. We generally provide copies of data in electronic form, unless you have specified otherwise. The right of access is subject to certain restrictions (see Art. 15(4) GDPR, section 34 BDSG).
Right to rectification: Under the conditions of Art. 16 GDPR, you may request the immediate rectification of inaccurate personal data or the completion of incomplete personal data.

Right to erasure: Under the conditions of Art. 17 GDPR, you may in principle request the erasure of your personal data stored by us. The right to erasure is subject to certain restrictions (see Art. 17(3) GDPR, section 35 BDSG).

Right to restriction of processing: Under the conditions of Art. 18 GDPR, you may also request the restriction of the processing of your personal data. In this case, we must restrict the data for the duration of the examination of your request.

Right to data portability: Under the conditions of Art. 20 GDPR, you have the right to receive the personal data you have provided to us in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format or, where technically feasible, to request its transmission to another controller, insofar as the processing is based on consent or a contract and is carried out by automated means. The right to data portability is subject to certain restrictions (see Art. 20(3) and (4) GDPR, section 28 BDSG).

Right to withdraw consent: Insofar as we process data on the basis of your consent, you may withdraw your consent at any time with effect for the future in accordance with Art. 7(3) GDPR. The withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of the processing carried out up to that point. Please address the withdrawal to the contact address provided under Section 2.
RIGHT TO OBJECT (ART. 21 GDPR)

YOU HAVE THE RIGHT TO OBJECT AT ANY TIME, ON GROUNDS RELATING TO YOUR PARTICULAR SITUATION, TO THE PROCESSING OF PERSONAL DATA CONCERNING YOU WHICH IS BASED ON ART. 6(1)(F) GDPR (LEGITIMATE INTERESTS). IN THE EVENT OF A JUSTIFIED OBJECTION, WE WILL CEASE THE PROCESSING CONCERNED UNLESS WE CAN DEMONSTRATE COMPELLING LEGITIMATE GROUNDS FOR THE PROCESSING WHICH OVERRIDE YOUR INTERESTS, RIGHTS AND FREEDOMS, OR THE PROCESSING SERVES THE ASSERTION, EXERCISE OR DEFENCE OF LEGAL CLAIMS.

WHERE YOUR PERSONAL DATA IS PROCESSED BY US FOR DIRECT MARKETING PURPOSES, YOU HAVE THE RIGHT TO OBJECT AT ANY TIME, WITHOUT RESTRICTION, TO THE PROCESSING OF YOUR DATA FOR SUCH MARKETING PURPOSES. IN THIS CASE, IT IS NOT NECESSARY TO STATE A PARTICULAR SITUATION. THIS ALSO APPLIES TO PROFILING TO THE EXTENT THAT IT IS RELATED TO SUCH DIRECT MARKETING. IF YOU OBJECT, THE PROCESSING FOR DIRECT MARKETING PURPOSES WILL BE CEASED IMMEDIATELY.
THE OBJECTION MAY BE MADE WITHOUT ANY PARTICULAR FORM (E.G. BY E-MAIL) TO THE CONTACT DETAILS PROVIDED UNDER SECTION 2.

content.title: 21. Right to Lodge a Complaint with a Supervisory Authority (Art. 77 GDPR)
paragraphs: If you are of the opinion that the processing of personal data concerning you by us violates data protection provisions, you have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority pursuant to Article 77 GDPR, in particular in the Member State of your habitual residence, your place of work or the place of the alleged infringement. 4.description: While heating or cooling is running, closed windows help the room reach and hold your temperature.
